title: AFTER — Research

body:
This part is not deep enough yet. That is probably the most important thing to say about it. I found sources. I organised sources. I can explain why they are relevant. That does not mean I understand them properly.

Some of the AI authorship papers went onto the board because the titles sounded almost exactly like what I was asking. That is not the same thing as reading the argument. I need to be more honest about that because I could easily make the research look much more finished than it is.

The identity side is where I started actually getting something back that complicated the question. If memory changes someone can still be recognised as themselves. If physical ability changes they are still themselves. Language can change. Accent can change. Opinions change. Culture and habits can change. Personality can change over time. So I keep having this instinct that there is some kind of core, but then what is the core? I do not actually know. And I should not make the project pretend I know.
The embodiment work was useful because it pushes against the easy idea that the real person is just somewhere inside the brain and the body is an accessory. Affect adds another issue because feeling is not necessarily something you can cleanly separate from identity either. I started getting different lenses instead of one answer, which is probably healthier for the project.

The authorship research also changed me more than I expected. I started this thinking authorship should be fully human. I do not really think that anymore. If I use something to help organise or expand what I am doing I do not think that automatically means authorship disappears.

The line has become harder to distinguish.

I think substitution starts happening when I cannot recognise my own voice, reasoning or decisions inside the thing anymore. For writing especially there is a difference between fixing a sentence I was struggling with and producing the thought for me. But even that is not perfectly clean. If I had the thought badly and something else expresses it better, whose articulation is it? Does authorship sit in the intention, the labour, the choices, the final wording, all of them?

I do not know yet honestly.

I also keep thinking about how polished AI answers feel. There is a certain surface where everything becomes too neatly organised. It starts sounding like there was always one straight direction through the thought when I do not really think that way. I jump, I backtrack, I contradict something and then come back to it. Sometimes that is because my writing is messy and should genuinely be improved. Sometimes that mess might be where the idea is still moving.

Art gave me another version of the same problem. If somebody erases a mark something happened between the thought and the hand. Maybe the mark did not translate what they wanted. Maybe it was ugly. Maybe they changed their mind. Maybe it means nothing psychologically at all. That is why I need to be careful with the art therapy material. It cannot become “AI can look at your drawing and discover your hidden self”. That would make the exact mistake I am trying to investigate.
Observation is not automatically interpretation. Interpretation is not automatically fact. Measurement is not automatically meaning.

That might become important later.

The next stage of the research has to be slower. Not another fifteen titles. Maybe three texts and actually arguing with them. What are they saying? What do I believe? What do I reject? What happens to the installation if they are right? What happens if they are wrong? Otherwise I am just collecting credible looking names around something I already wanted to say.

One sentence I would keep: I do not need research to prove my project. I need it to make the question harder for me to answer.
